Figure 1. Proposed Heartverse framework for developmental physiology-guided ECG augmentation and pediatric arrhythmia detection. (A) Pediatric ECGs are harmonized and split by patient before segmentation. Adult-to-child transferability is a supporting investigation. Generator A uses age conditioning, whereas generator B additionally uses developmental physiology and simulation. Both share the same real training patients, backbone and training budget. The same classifier is trained separately on real ECGs only, real plus A, or real plus B, with conventional augmentation as an additional baseline. (B) Exact age, rhythm labels and shared patient metadata condition generation. Normal training ECGs and published age references define developmental profiles that guide physiological simulation while preserving the intended abnormal rhythm. Planned and error-targeted allocation are evaluated with both generators; targeting uses training-internal validation. Synthetic counts and age-rhythm composition are matched between generators within each allocation strategy. (C) Study findings, classification performance and retrospective review-prioritization outcomes are reported by age group and rhythm on held-out real patients. All label-dependent components respect the same pediatric label budget. Missed cases, false alarms and review workload are assessed using observed test prevalence and validation-set thresholds.

Ages 1-16 years are the proposed scope; final age coverage and group boundaries depend on available patients and reliable rhythm labels. Exact age guides generation, while age groups summarize evaluation; axis ticks indicate age values rather than fixed group boundaries. The figure depicts a proposed study, and its signals, distributions and model blocks are schematic rather than empirical results. Demonstrating clinical decision benefit requires a clinician reader study or prospective evaluation.
